criteria.criterion: The producer brief in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs (producer_brief_with_evidence) has a new 'Time budget' section giving the producer's deadline in seconds, taken from the configured producer deadline and not a constant, and telling it to finish the smallest complete change first, run the full test suite at most once, and keep the tree reportable. Verify by reading the diff.
criteria.evidence: I read the diff and briefs.rs:684-756. `time_budget_section(deadline_s)` builds its text from its argument and contains no number literal for the limit. It is called unconditionally at briefs.rs:696, after pin_section and before failure_classes_section. `deadline_s` is filled at run/mod.rs:1224 from `producer::producer_deadline_s(&jc)`, which returns `jc.config.budget.producer_timeout_s` (producer.rs:49-51). The invocation uses the same accessor at producer.rs:350, inside the send-back loop, so every pass runs under that limit. The text tells the producer to do the smallest change that meets every acceptance criterion first, to run the full suite at most once, and to leave no half-edited file or broken build between steps. The sections it points to ('Commands Bash may run', 'Checks before the verifier') are rendered below it, at briefs.rs:710 and 749.

criteria.criterion: A new unit test in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs fails on the base and passes with the change. It builds producer briefs for two different deadlines and asserts each brief states its own deadline value, and that the section appears for a fresh job, a retry and a resume. Run: cargo test -p athena-context.
criteria.evidence: `time_budget_states_each_jobs_own_deadline` passed when I ran it. It checks deadlines of 300 and 5400, each present in its own brief and absent from the other. It also checks five brief shapes (fresh, seeded retry, resume, stale conflict, unseeded retry), each with exactly one '## Time budget' section. Athena's fails-without-2 record shows the test does not compile on the base (no `deadline_s` field, exit 101). With the field present but a constant in the text, the 5400 assertion would still catch it.

criteria.criterion: A test in crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs shows the deadline configured for the producer invocation is the number written into the stored brief-producer.md (the same value, not a copy). Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
criteria.evidence: The test passed in 7.69s. It sets producer_timeout_s = 4321 in the test repository's athena.toml and runs ask and go to a landed job. It then asserts that 4321 is the invocation's timeout (spec.timeout), the producer invocation record's caps.timeout_s and the job's caps.producer_timeout_s. It also asserts that the stored brief-producer's Time budget section says '4321 seconds' and is identical to the section in the prompt the producer received, that the stored brief does not contain '86400', and that the prompt is the stored brief with only the evidence path filled in. Athena's fails-without-3 record shows exit 101 with the fix reverted.

criteria.criterion: Root cause named in CHANGELOG.md and in the doc comment of the new section: the stage lacked its own deadline and pacing information. Jobs 20261010-154006-vc5k, 20261016-052605-qw38 and 20261018-070117-qmxv are addressed by this: they recorded no candidate, so nothing is kept from them. Their original requests (verifier snapshot note, auditor and warden roles, baseline checks) are not part of this change.
criteria.evidence: The new CHANGELOG bullet under Added says: 'the producer stage was never told its own per-run limit, so it could not pace against it'. It names all three jobs, says they recorded no candidate so nothing is kept from them, and says their requests (verifier snapshot note, auditor and warden roles, baseline checks) are not redone. The doc comment on `time_budget_section` (briefs.rs:758-762) names the same root cause. The entry also notes that the live limit is 86400 s (athena.toml:51 confirms it), that the producer has no `date` command (athena.toml grants none), and that the stall window is one third of the limit (procs.rs:30 confirms it).

criteria.criterion: No refusal rule is added: nothing in the diff refuses, holds or rejects a reading or job. Expected 0% of newly refused readings.
criteria.evidence: The production changes are one brief section, one ProducerInputs field, one accessor and one field assignment. No error, bail, hold or reject path is added, and check_reading_size is unchanged. Athena's replay found 0 of 50 accepted readings newly refused.

criteria.criterion: Outcome check for the producer-deadline-exceeded-on-small-job class: running cargo test shows the brief of a small job (short deadline and one deliverable) carries the budget text, so the producer is told its limit before it starts.

findings.summary: Whether the brief text actually prevents deadline failures is not measured, and at today's limit it is weak.
findings.evidence: The live limit is 86400 s (athena.toml:51), so today the brief tells producers 86400 seconds. The failure class was observed under 1800 s. The entry says this itself ('Whether producers follow the text is not measured'). This is an honest limit, not a defect, but the fix only shows its effect if the limit is lowered again. A follow-up could count deadline failures after landing.

findings.summary: The CHANGELOG entry is very long for one bullet.
findings.evidence: One paragraph of about 400 words holds the root cause, the fix, the limits and the test commands. A shorter bullet that points to the tests would be easier to read.

summary: The change passes. It fixes the root cause where it starts, in the producer's inputs: the producer brief now has a `## Time budget` section that states the producer's own limit in seconds and how to pace against it. The number comes from `producer_deadline_s(jc)`, the same accessor that sets the invocation's timeout, so the limit the brief states cannot drift from the one enforced. The section appears in every brief shape (fresh job, retry, stale conflict, resume). I ran the three new tests and all passed. `time_budget_states_each_jobs_own_deadline` checks two deadlines across five brief shapes. `a_small_job_brief_carries_its_short_deadline` checks a one-deliverable job with a 120-second limit. The athena-core end-to-end test checks that a configured 4321 s is the invocation's timeout, appears in the recorded caps and appears in the stored brief-producer.md. Athena's fails-without runs show that the tests for criteria 2 and 3 fail with the fix reverted (they do not compile, exit 101). fmt, clippy and test passed according to Athena's recorded CI checks. No refusal rule is added, and all six changed files are on the deliverables list. One honest limit, which the CHANGELOG states itself: whether producers follow the text is not measured, and at today's 86400-second limit the stated number matters little.
